answer: Take a submission, hand it to three peers who never worked together, and release payment only when all three reproduce the same output hash. Renaming an account buys nothing because the check replays the receipt itself. In one audit a copied claim surfaced when two peers in different regions produced different hashes from it. A clean run shows up as three matching hashes, a jade ledger line and a plume of signed receipts in the log. The velvet lining is the latency, since three confirmations slow every payout. The open question is who absorbs that wait when the work is urgent.
